Run cleangrowth() with automatic checkpointing (deprecated wrapper)

Source: R/cleangrowth_checkpoint.R
cleangrowth_checkpoint.Rd

Deprecated. Checkpointing is built into cleangrowth via its checkpoint_dir argument – call cleangrowth(data, checkpoint_dir = ...) directly. This wrapper forwards to cleangrowth() and will be removed in a future version. The use_existing_checkpoint_results argument maps to cleangrowth(checkpoint_resume = ...). Calling cleangrowth() directly also lets a checkpointed run use wide / semi-wide input and output (via its input_format / output_format).

Usage

cleangrowth_checkpoint(
  data,
  checkpoint_dir,
  checkpoint_size = 5000,
  log_file = NULL,
  keep_checkpoints = TRUE,
  use_existing_checkpoint_results = FALSE,
  quietly = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data, checkpoint_dir, checkpoint_size, log_file, keep_checkpoints, quietly, verbose

See cleangrowth. quietly defaults to FALSE here (this wrapper prints by default).

use_existing_checkpoint_results

Deprecated alias for cleangrowth(checkpoint_resume = ...): reuse existing checkpoint files (resume an interrupted run) instead of starting fresh.

...

Additional arguments passed to cleangrowth (e.g. cf_rescue, sd.recenter, adult_permissiveness).

Value

A data.table – see cleangrowth for the output columns.

See also

cleangrowth, cleangrowth_checkpoint_combine

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(data.table)
dt <- fread("large_dataset.csv")

# Preferred: call cleangrowth() directly with checkpoint_dir.
result <- cleangrowth(dt, checkpoint_dir = "results/gc_checkpoints",
                      checkpoint_size = 5000, log_file = "results/gc_run.log")
} # }
